members.duties: mechanics audit: damage-budget compliance (flat numbers on Novice 2/4/6, Adept 6/9/12, Master 9/15/21), prereq shapes (Adept exactly 2, Master exactly 3), cost math (cards 2/4/8), level gates, dice remnants, stale vocabulary, cross-chapter contradictions
consistency and voice: repeated phrases, tonal drift, name collisions, redundant sections, flavor-vs-rules balance
final quality: structure, cross-references, missing content, completeness
presentation: Quarto/Typst render, heading hierarchy, table formatting/overflow, typography, page flow, card layout, reference-sheet usability, em-dash law

payload.name: hol-rulebook
payload.problem_domain: Heroes of Legend TTRPG rulebook chapter review and disposition

payload.statement:
# HOL Council — ch01 Introduction

Chapter under review: ch01 (quarto-book/chapters/01-introduction.qmd), "Introduction", 243 lines.
The player-facing introduction: welcome, what you need, how to read the book, the core 3d6
mechanic (Weak/Standard/Strong, Critical, Fumble), the always-hit rule, a worked example of
play (Kael and Lyra in a goblin ruin), and designer justifications (why 3d6, why always-hit,
no spell slots, flat damage, disciplines).

Task: audit the chapter as a publishable unit and produce a disposition plan.
Each member audits through their own lens (see role card) and files ONE finding:
  stance support = the chapter holds on this lens as written
  stance refute  = the chapter must change; name the fix and its scope
Findings cite [file:line] in 01-introduction.qmd. Mechanics findings state the broken value and
the expected value. Cross-chapter checks use the AUTHORITATIVE chapters as the reference, not
this chapter:

  opening fiction = ch01b (The Last Ember): the Kael/Lyra/Roric/Zara party and how each character
    actually plays in-story is the canon reference for the worked example at lines 144-181.
    ch01 names Kael's and Lyra's ancestry+class at line 146; verify them against how ch01b
    portrays them (Kael = Blade, Lyra = Odd, and the specific disciplines/abilities each shows).
  core resolution = ch06: 3d6 core roll, success tiers 1-8/9-14/15-18+, Critical (three natural
    6s), Fumble (three natural 1s), always-hit attacks.
  damage = ch08: flat budgets Novice 2/4/6, Adept 6/9/12, Master 9/15/21, one-roll principle.
    The worked example's numbers (longsword damage + Brawn, then DR reduction) must be on-table
    flat values, not dice.
  armor/DR = ch16: leather armor DR.
  advancement = ch18: levels 1-10, Adept gate L3, Master gate L7.

Book conventions every lens applies: flat damage budgets only (no damage dice), card costs
2/4/8 DP, Adept prereq exactly 2 ranks, Master exactly 3, ZERO em-dashes in the book, no stale
or retired vocabulary, placeholder captions consistent with the rest of the book, and worked
examples that stay tier-correct (a Standard roll must map to a Standard damage row).

Disposition tiers the final recommendation must use:
  TIER 1 mechanical — chapter-local, no mechanics change, no content judgment.
  TIER 2 substantive — content rewrites, cross-chapter reconciliation.
  TIER 3 design-decision — design-authority questions for the lead designer.
Also flag any finding that is a BOOK-WIDE convention (visible in sibling chapters), because a
chapter-local fix would make ch01 inconsistent with the book; those route to a convention
decision, not a single-chapter edit.

payload.argument: The worked example that teaches combat arithmetic uses a damage-reduction value that contradicts the book's armor table. The chieftain's gear is described as leather and the example subtracts one point [01-introduction.qmd:160], but the authoritative armor chapter lists leather at two [16-armor-shields.qmd:34], and that chapter's own Kael example likewise uses two [16-armor-shields.qmd:23]. A first-time player who learns the math here will find the numbers disagree the moment they open the armor chapter, which defeats the introduction's purpose of modeling the system. Fix: change the example's reduction to 2 and recompute the final damage from 2 to 1, or alternatively relabel the armor as the table's only DR-1 entry (Padded) so the arithmetic holds; scope is one line, two tokens. This is the single defect that breaks the chapter as a publishable unit on the documentation lens: I also verified the cross-reference targets, tier bands, class roster, example roll math, the 2/4/6 standard value, and the per-encounter/per-session spell limits, and each reconciles with its authoritative chapter; adjacent mismatches worth noting but not dispositive are the credits-page art embedded mid-chapter at [01-introduction.qmd:88-90] and the bestiary's goblin entry showing DR 0 rather than any leather. The deliberation should settle on ch16 as the source of truth for this example and correct ch01 to match.

evidence.claim: The worked example reduces the chieftain's incoming damage from 3 to 2 by applying a reduction of 1 to his leather armor [01-introduction.qmd:160].

The armor table assigns leather a reduction of 2 [16-armor-shields.qmd:34], and the same chapter's Kael example applies 2 to leather, so the authoritative value conflicts with the introduction's 1 [16-armor-shields.qmd:23].

The introduction's arithmetic is only self-consistent if the reduction is 2 (then the final value is 1) or if the armor is relabeled to the table's sole DR-1 entry; either edit touches one line and two tokens in ch01, with no effect on any other chapter.
evidence.quote_or_excerpt: 3 - 2 = 1; the line must read reduced to 1

payload.argument: The worked example's second roll silently assumes a character level the chapter never establishes, and it does so on a line the intro is the first place a new player sees the tiered skill system. At [01-introduction.qmd:173] Lyra adds 'Stealth Adept +2' to her roll. Per the skill ladder an Adept skill bonus (+2) is gated to Level 3 ([07-skills.qmd:28]; [18-advancement.qmd:45]), and creation rules state a Level-1 hero cannot hold any Adept-tier thing ([02-character-creation.qmd:113]). The example gives no level for the party. Worse, the chapter's own onboarding copy [01-introduction.qmd:80] primes the reader to treat these as brand-new, first-session characters, so the first concrete example they copy from already shows a Level-3+ bonus. Counter-example I tested: a table that reads only ch01 and builds its heroes at Level 1 will hit 'Adept' in the example, have no in-chapter definition of what Adept means for skills, and either (a) copy a +2 bonus they cannot legally have, or (a) stop trusting the example. The example also teaches the Adept/Master ladder as a flat list without ever stating the level gates that ch07/ch18 attach to it. This is a rules-lawyer seam and an unexamined assumption, exactly the worked-example defect the brief targets. Fix (scope: chapter-local, Tier 1, no mechanics change): in the example at line 173, either (a) state the party's level so 'Stealth Adept +2' is lawful, or (b) downgrade Lyra to a Novice-consistent roll (e.g. Stealth Novice +1, total 16) so the example models a Level-1 party, and add one sentence to the 'How to Read the Roll' section that skill tiers unlock by level (Novice at 1, Adept at 3, Master at 7). The 3d6 core, success tiers, Critical/Fumble, and always-hit are untouched.

evidence.claim: Lyra's example roll adds an Adept-tier skill bonus (+2) to reach a Strong result, with no party level stated anywhere in the example.
The skill tier table gates the Adept (+2) bonus behind Level 3, so a +2 skill bonus is unavailable to a starting hero.
The advancement table confirms Adept abilities (and by the same ladder, Adept skills) unlock at Level 3, matching the skill chapter.
Character creation states a Level-1 hero is a Novice and cannot hold Adept- or Master-tier content, so the example's +2 presumes a level the intro never sets.
evidence.quote_or_excerpt: At Level 1, you are a Novice.

evidence.claim: The onboarding copy frames the reader as a first-time player, which makes the first worked example the model they will copy, amplifying the unexamined level assumption.
evidence.quote_or_excerpt: If you've never rolled a d20 in your life

payload.argument: Fact-checking ch01's three risky areas against the authoritative chapters surfaced no defects. The worked example at 01-introduction.qmd:156-160 reproduces the canonical ch06 resolution example step for step: a 13 Standard maps to the card's Standard row (2) plus Brawn (+1) for 3, and crude-leather DR 1 leaves 2. The ancestry-plus-class labels on Kael and Lyra at line 146 match independent labels in ch03, ch07 and ch13, and ch01b's own class signals. Every @sec-chapter-* anchor ch01 cites resolves to a defined #label in the target chapter.

evidence.claim: The authoritative core-resolution worked example uses the same fight and identical arithmetic ch01 dramatizes: 12 plus Brawn 1 is Standard, the card Standard row is 2 plus Brawn 1, and DR 1 reduces it to 2.
Basic Melee's printed Standard row is the flat 2-plus-Brawn value ch01 applies, so the example's damage is an on-card number, not a damage-dice roll.
The attributes chapter independently names Lyra as halfling and Odd, corroborating the identity ch01 gives her at line 146.
The skills chapter independently names Kael as dwarf and Blade, corroborating ch01's line 146 identification.
The combat chapter's surprise-check example uses the identical Lyra stat block ch01 uses (Agility +2, Stealth Adept +2, total 19 Strong), so the example hero matches the canon build.
The opening fiction's own class markers match ch01's labels: Kael performs the Blade role and Lyra the Odd role in-story.
evidence.quote_or_excerpt: The Odd didn't follow the rules of magic

evidence.claim: Grep of the chapters directory shows every label ch01 references (character-creation, attributes, disciplines, gm-guidance, armor-shields, core-resolution, magic-system, combat) exists as a #label in its chapter; no dangling cross-reference found.
evidence.quote_or_excerpt: all eight referenced chapter labels resolve to real anchors

payload.argument: In the tutorial fight the chieftain's crude leather is assigned DR 1, so Kael's 3-damage Standard blow is reported as landing for 2 [01-introduction.qmd:160]. The armor canon rates Leather at DR 2, so the blow should land for 1. The identical off-table DR 1 is duplicated in the matching scene at ch06:197, meaning a chapter-local edit alone would leave the book internally inconsistent; the correction needs to be applied to both chapters.

evidence.claim: The armor table rates Leather at DR 2, and that chapter's own worked example uses DR 2 for Kael's leather.
Line 160's tutorial credits the chieftain's leather with DR 1 and reports the 3-damage hit reduced to 2.
evidence.quote_or_excerpt: Crude leather armor. DR 1. That's 3, reduced to 2.

evidence.claim: The equipment chapter's armor list also sets Leather at DR 2.
The same goblin-chieftain example appears there with the identical DR 1, so the value is a shared defect rather than a chapter-local slip.
evidence.quote_or_excerpt: The chieftain's crude leather gives DR 1

evidence.claim: Under the canonical Leather DR 2 the example's 3 damage is reduced to 1, not 2.

payload.argument: The Kael sentence at [01-introduction.qmd:146] fails on two independent author-lens grounds and must change. (1) Repeated stock phrase: its Kael tagline is a near-verbatim lift of the Blade class's signature line in [05-classes.qmd:84]; the same two-part image (wall shadow plus final face seen) appears only twice in the whole book and both times in this construction, so the Introduction burns the Classes chapter's signature image two chapters early, leaving the class page to repeat what the reader already owns. (2) Character-description inconsistency: the intro itself points readers to the opening story as where they will meet Kael and Lyra, yet the line 146 description contradicts Kael's canonical behavior there. In [01b-opening-fiction.qmd:27] and [01b-opening-fiction.qmd:45] he is the forward decoy: he leads through the breach with his blade alight, and the fiction explicitly states his role as drawing attention, making the opening, and trusting an ally to finish the kill. That is the first face the enemy sees, played loudly and visibly, the opposite of a hidden wall shadow whose final image is the strike itself. The worked example that follows reinforces this: it is Lyra, not Kael, who performs the stealth move. Minimal fix, scoped to one sentence: rewrite the Kael clause at line 146 to match the ch01b portrayal (vanguard who draws the eye; optionally the flaming blade), and let the shadow/last-face line belong to the Blade entry in ch05 alone. Do not demand a rewrite of ch01b or ch05.

evidence.claim: The flagged sentence: a dwarf Blade defined by the wall-shadow image and the last-face image, then precision striking, then the promise that readers meet these two in the opening story.
evidence.quote_or_excerpt: a shadow on the wall, the last face his enemies see

evidence.claim: The Blade class entry carries the same two-part image as its signature line, which the intro sentence pre-empts nearly verbatim.
evidence.quote_or_excerpt: the shadow on the wall, the final face your enemies see

evidence.claim: Canon behavior: Kael leads through the breach, blade on fire, and the fiction states his role as drawing the eye, making the opening, and trusting someone else to finish.
evidence.quote_or_excerpt: The Blade draws the eye. The Blade makes the opening

evidence.claim: In the worked example directly below the flagged sentence, it is Lyra who makes the stealth move while Kael steps forward and strikes openly, confirming the stealth image does not belong to Kael in this book's own example.
evidence.quote_or_excerpt: I want to slip behind the throne

payload.argument: The chapter's final call-to-action box names the game-master role with the retired label 'GM' at [01-introduction.qmd:236], but the book has standardized on the invented term Dungeon Architect (DA). The same chapter establishes that term three times earlier (line 17 'Dungeon Architect (DA)', line 33 'the Dungeon Architect (the DA)', line 82 'If you're the Dungeon Architect'), the ch19 chapter is titled 'Dungeon Architect's Guide', and the ch21 glossary defines the role as 'DA (Dungeon Architect): The game master'. A first-time reader who was just told at line 82 to read 'If you're the Dungeon Architect' then meets a fresh 'New GM?' bullet at line 236 and must work out that GM and DA are the same seat, which is avoidable friction in the welcome-to-the-table moment. This is stale vocabulary plus an internal inconsistency, not a mechanics issue. Fix and scope: rename the line-236 bullet heading from 'New GM?' to 'New Dungeon Architect?' (or 'New DA?') so the closing pointers match the terminology the rest of the chapter and book already use. Single-line, chapter-local, TIER 1; no content or rule change. Every other quality check passed: all ten distinct @sec-chapter-* cross-references resolve to defined anchors in their target chapters, and the worked example is arithmetically and tier-consistent with ch09 Basic Melee and ch06.

evidence.claim: The closing bullet uses the retired GM label for the game-master seat, which the book has otherwise replaced with its own term.
The same chapter already establishes the canonical role name and abbreviation earlier, making the later GM an outlier within one chapter.
The glossary fixes the authoritative label for the role, confirming GM is not a book term.
Renaming the one bullet to the established term removes the stale vocabulary and the within-chapter mismatch with zero impact on mechanics or scope.
evidence.quote_or_excerpt: GM is the sole outlier here

payload.argument: The figure at 01-introduction.qmd:88-90 is captioned as the Credits page's artwork, yet it is stranded on its own page in the middle of the Introduction, boxed between forced page breaks (lines 86 and 92) directly ahead of '## The Core Mechanic', while the real Credits page in the front matter (00-front-matter.qmd:37-51) carries no artwork at all. Nothing in the surrounding prose (lines 84-94) refers to the image, no in-text reference ties it to the chapter, and it is one of only two figures in the chapter with empty alt text (both legacy page003 imports, unlike every real placeholder). A reader told this depicts the credits page will never find it there. Fix: relocate the figure and caption onto ch00's Credits page (after its credits list) and renumber ch01's opening-art caption at line 9 from 'Illustration 2' to 'Illustration 3'; no later illustration numbers change because the insertion point precedes them. Alternatively, if a transition piece is genuinely intended at this spot, recaption the figure to describe what it actually depicts there. Scope: 01-introduction.qmd lines 88-90 (and 00-front-matter.qmd plus the line-9 renumber if relocation is chosen).

evidence.claim: The chapter's third illustration caption identifies the artwork as belonging to the Credits page, but the figure occupies its own full page between two forced page breaks immediately before the core-mechanic section (lines 88-92), with no prose reference and no alt text.
evidence.quote_or_excerpt: Illustration 3: Credits page art. Placeholder; final art TBD.

evidence.claim: The front matter's Credits page (lines 37-51) is a plain text block holding no figure, so the artwork the caption names as credits-page art has no home where a reader would expect to find it.

File name and measured pixel size (1024x1024, page003-img003.jpeg) match the caption, confirming the artifact is the legacy credits-page import; since the figure's current slot precedes all later illustration numbers, relocating it to ch00 changes only ch01's own line-9 caption, keeping the fix small and contained.
evidence.quote_or_excerpt: captioned front-matter art stranded mid-chapter on a card page

dissent.position: Fact-checked ch01's risky areas (worked-example math, Kael/Lyra identities, cross-reference anchors) against the authoritative chapters and found them consistent: the example reproduces the canonical ch06 resolution, the identities match ch03/ch07/ch13, and every @sec-chapter-* anchor resolves. Voted support on that verification; did not weigh the armor-table contradiction because the DR value the librarian and game-architect flagged sits in the shared ch06 example, which the researcher took as authoritative rather than checking against the ch16 armor table itself.

payload.rationale: The round-1 verdict is unambiguous: 6 of 7 members refute topic t-01 and none rebutted (reject quorum 4 was reached in a single round). Independent verification confirmed the load-bearing claims. f-001 (librarian) and f-004 (game-architect) independently converged on the same DR defect from different directions (documentation-coherence vs armor canon): the tutorial's 'crude leather DR 1' contradicts the ch16 table's Leather DR 2, and the same error is duplicated in the matching scene at ch06:197, so the fix must touch both chapters atomically. f-005 (author) verified ch01:146's near-verbatim lift of the ch05:86 Blade signature and its mismatch with Kael's ch01b fire-blade vanguard portrayal. f-006 (editor-in-chief) verified the 'New GM?' retired-label defect at ch01:236 against the chapter's own DA usage. f-007 (layout-expert) verified the stranded 'Illustration 3: Credits page art' orphan against ch00's artless Credits page. f-002 (contrarian) raised the Adept-gating question at ch01:173; the researcher's verification (f-003) that Lyra's Adept Stealth is her canonical ch13 stat block and that all @sec-* anchors resolve was accepted, so the contrarian item is dispositioned as a clarity note rather than a stat change. The two support-lens verdicts were for different scopes: game-architect and editor-in-chief refuted on their specific findings even where the chapter's core structure (mechanics, cross-refs) is sound.
payload.recommendation: VERDICT: REJECTED 6-1. Six voters (librarian, contrarian, game-architect, author, editor-in-chief, layout-expert) refuted topic t-01; one (researcher) supported; none rebutted; no impasse, no judge sat. ch01 (quarto-book/chapters/01-introduction.qmd) does not publish as written: its tutorial combat arithmetic teaches a leather DR that contradicts the armor canon, its hero tagline lifts the Blade class signature nearly verbatim, and it uses a retired role label. Execute this TIERED DISPOSITION PLAN, built on dispositions independently verified against the book chapters and the built PDF (source of record). TIER 1 (mechanical, zero mechanics change, fix directly in a micro-PR on quarto-book/chapters/01-introduction.qmd): (1) ch01:236 'New GM?' uses the retired game-master label; the book standardizes on Dungeon Architect (DA) — ch01 itself establishes DA three times earlier (lines 17, 30, 82), ch19 is 'Dungeon Architect's Guide', ch21 glossary defines DA. Change the closing-box bullet to 'New DA?'. (2) ch01:88-90: the figure captioned 'Illustration 3: Credits page art' is an orphaned legacy asset (page003-img003.jpeg, empty alt text) stranded on its own page between two forced pagebreaks mid-Introduction; ch00's real Credits page (00-front-matter.qmd:37-51) carries no artwork, so the caption's named home does not exist. Remove the stranded figure + pagebreak sandwich so The Core Mechanic flows after the intro prose; the asset stays in assets/images for a future Credits-page placement decision. (3) ch01:146: the Kael tagline 'a shadow on the wall, the last face his enemies see' is a near-verbatim lift of the Blade class signature in ch05:86 ('You are the shadow on the wall, the final face your enemies see'), which burns the class page's signature image two chapters early, and it contradicts Kael's actual ch01b portrayal (fire-touched longsword, first through the breach, draws the eye). Rework the sentence so it is not a lift and matches the fiction's Kael. TIER 2 (substantive, canon-determined by ch16 armor table, fix directly in the same micro-PR on both files - the finding defines scope, not the file): (4) ch01:160 AND ch06:197 both credit the goblin chieftain's crude leather with DR 1 (3 reduced to 2), but ch16's armor table (16-armor-shields.qmd:34) rates Leather at DR 2 and ch16's own Kael example (line 23) applies DR 2 to leather; ch15 equipment agrees. The tutorial must match the armor canon or a first-time player's arithmetic is wrong the moment they open ch16. Atomic two-file edit: ch01:160 and ch06:197 change to DR 2 with the damage recomputed to 1 (3-2=1), keeping 'crude leather' as the evocative label (a cheap leather is still leather, DR 2). TIER 3 (design-flavored, implement recommended default anchored on canon and log in decisions-pending.md as 'implemented default 2026-09-03, veto to revert'): (5) ch01:173 Lyra's roll adds 'Stealth Adept +2', which per ch07:28/ch18:45 is gated to level 3; the chapter never states the party's level, and the onboarding copy (ch01:80) primes new players, so a first-session reader cannot tell the +2 is lawful. Her Adept Stealth is canon (ch13:432 uses the identical stat block; ch01b's party is clearly not first-level - Zara has three Wind Disciplines), so the recommended default is a one-clause clarity note in the example intro that Kael and Lyra are veteran adventurers (several levels in), making the Adept bonus lawful and teaching the gate, rather than downgrading her stat block (which would contradict ch13). Also log for Bruce (open question, not implemented): the deeper Blade-class identity tension surfaced by the author lens - ch01b:45 frames the Blade as the vanguard who draws the eye and makes the opening, while ch05:83-86 frames the Blade as the shadow-assassin ('the shadow on the wall, the final face your enemies see') who favors light blades; Kael canonically carries a longsword. That is a ch05/ch01b class-identity question for the lead designer, out of scope for a ch01 edit.

resolved.outcome: rejected 6-1 - chapter does not publish as written; proceed with the tiered disposition plan (3 Tier-1 chapter-local fixes + 1 Tier-2 two-file canon fix in one micro-PR, 1 Tier-3 implemented default logged in decisions-pending.md, 1 open design question logged for Bruce)
